note: Both bullets proven. AES GCM bullet: TestRFC5282AEADEncryptionKeysCarryTheirSalt (20/36 octets, key-then-salt round trip). AES CCM bullet: new TestRFC5282CCMEncryptionKeysCarryTheirSalt, every CCM ID at 128/256 bits: SK_ei and SK_er are exactly cipher key + 3 octets (19/35), and a SealIKEAEAD output is opened by a ccm instance built in the test from key[:n] with nonce = trailing 3 salt octets || 8-octet IV, which is the RFC 4309 Section 7.1 KEYMAT format and Section 4 nonce; a 4-octet GCM salt or salt-first layout fails the length or the open. Negative: TestRFC5282NonAEADEncryptionKeysCarryNoSalt. Records: SealIKEAEAD and encKeyMaterialLen reverts observed red. Residual: the opener uses ze's own internal/core/ccm package, so it checks the key split, not the CCM primitive itself.
